nodes.reason: S2.p2.1 explicitly defines the full real matrix orthogonal group by transpose(O) O = I. No determinant constraint is imposed in that definition.

The finite real matrix subspace topology and its Borel sigma-algebra are the standard interpretation of this Haar background object. Hausdorffness, second countability and the topological-group structure are background obligations, not author-proved results in S2.
Finite real orthogonal matrices form a closed bounded set; identity supplies a point. Compactness and nonemptiness explicate standard background, including the singleton dimension-zero case.
Existence is standard Haar theory applied to this locally compact group. It is correctly marked a construction obligation rather than a source author theorem.
On the nonempty compact full group, a Haar measure has finite positive total mass, so normalization on univ yields probability. The normalization is not on SO(n) or a determinant component.

Standard uniqueness up to scalar together with total mass one fixes the measure. The canonical compact metrizable Borel setting removes a nonregular-measure ambiguity; this is background semantics, not implementation verification.
The first sentence of S2.p2.1 supplies precisely the full-group Haar probability object. Its component-conditioned objects occur in later sentences and are separate.
Left translation by fixed Q preserves Haar measure. The pushforward direction O -> Q O is the direction actually needed for A2.Ex53.m1.
A2.SS2.p2.1 explicitly says O is Haar distributed on the full orthogonal group, with n >= 3. This marginal draw is not the conditioned law mu_(n,b).
A2.SS2.SSS1.p3.1 defines D_i for an index i >= 2 belonging to S; A2.Ex53.m1 first equality states D_i O has O's law. This is fixed left multiplication, not conjugation or right multiplication.
S4.SS1.p1.1 gives d >= 2 and S4.SS1.p1.2 draws O from Haar(O(d)). The law is the same dimension-indexed full-group background object; independence from the private seed is separate.

S4.SS1.p1.2 sets A = O Lambda O^T, and S4.SS1.p2.1 identifies O as the unknown eigenbasis. This is an actual separate consumer of the marginal law, not a theorem transferring the determinant experiment.

explicit_exclusions.item: two determinant components and their mass 1/2
explicit_exclusions.reason: S2.p2.1 states two components and half mass, but that is a separate positive-dimension theorem. The all-natural-dimension interface does not carry it to n = 0.
The final sentence of S2.p2.1 defines a conditional law. Neither this object nor conditioning correctness follows from the reviewed full-marginal interface alone.

explicit_exclusions.item: row reflection preserves O_11, flips a principal minor, and gives zero expectation
explicit_exclusions.locator: A2.Ex53.m1 second and third equalities; A2.Ex54
explicit_exclusions.reason: The second and third equalities in A2.Ex53.m1 and the subsequent A2.Ex54 expectation argument require separate matrix algebra and integration. They remain outside this graph.

explicit_exclusions.item: Lemma B.6 determinant cancellation and signed Gaussian expectations
explicit_exclusions.reason: B.2.1 identifies Lemma B.6 and A2.E15 as the signed determinant/Gaussian cancellation result. Only one invariant-law input to its proof is reviewed here.

explicit_exclusions.item: independence of Haar O from private random seed
explicit_exclusions.reason: S4.SS1.p1.2 explicitly adds independence from private randomness. A marginal Haar law does not establish that joint-law assertion.

explicit_exclusions.item: conditional Haar residual laws, adaptive posterior, Haar revelation/state
explicit_exclusions.reason: The A2.SS1 and A3.SS1 references and A3.Thmtheorem1-3 identify distinct indistinguishability, conditional Haar revelation/state, and adaptive obligations. Their proofs are neither supplied nor reviewed.
Section 4.1 is used only to identify the separate Haar eigenbasis consumer. No Krylov/Gaussian experiment or Appendix C reduction follows merely from sharing this marginal object.

explicit_exclusions.item: main lower bounds and mixture/separation experiments
explicit_exclusions.reason: Section 2 oracle/accuracy definitions and the named downstream branches do not turn this background graph into a proof of main lower bounds or mixture separation. Those arguments remain excluded.

graph_audit.branch_structure: The determinant and eigenbasis branches are separate consumers of the same dimension-indexed full Haar law. There is no joining edge or AND requirement between their experiments. The two inputs to row_reflection_invariant_law belong to the same B.2.1 use site.
graph_audit.source_vs_background: The graph correctly labels canonical topology, compactness, Haar existence, normalization and uniqueness as standard background obligations. S2 introduces the background object; it does not present these constructions as author theorems.
graph_audit.dimension_boundary: The packet discloses generalization to every natural n. At n = 0, the empty-matrix orthogonal group is a singleton and its Haar probability is the unique probability on that singleton. No two-component or half-mass assertion is accepted there. Actual source use ranges remain n >= 3 in B.2 and d >= 2 in Section 4.1.

truth_boundary.accepted_claim: The sealed topology graph faithfully records the selected full-group Haar background object, its standard construction/characterization obligations, the actual left-reflection distributional use, and the separate Section 4.1 eigenbasis consumer, with the stated exclusions.
truth_boundary.limitation: Acceptance is source alignment and dependency-topology acceptance only. Embedded proposed Lean statements and definitions were considered for their declared mathematical meaning, never checked against implementation, Mathlib, proof terms, or compilation.
